hypothesis: On two toy systems instantiating a discovery-shaped deletion-and-repair move, no single execution-free nominator ranks the load-bearing deletion highly on both, and a max-disjunction of weakness gain and cost attribution is at least as good as the better single nominator on each.

controls.description: Seeded random ordering of candidate deletions.
Degenerate nominator preferring larger deletions; should lose whenever ranking does real work.
Propositions whose deletion frees nothing (invariant mass, orientation, bounded state) are scored rather than filtered, so the recall denominator is meaningful.
The child task cannot separate the held representation from the target member; verified by a regression test.
Ties broken by seeded shuffle rather than name, so a silent nominator scores at chance instead of inheriting alphabetical credit.

gates.criterion: On toy_kinematics weakness ranks a load-bearing deletion in its top-3 while cost does not, AND on toy_transduction cost does while weakness does not.
The disjunctive nominator attains D-recall@3 at least equal to the better of weakness and cost on both toys.
At least one of weakness or cost strictly beats both the random and size_only controls on at least one toy.
A nominator whose scores are entirely tied must score at chance; deterministic name-ordered tie-breaking is forbidden because it leaks whatever the sort key correlates with.
